persona.label: Unclear and disorganised
persona.description: Hard to interview. Rambles, misreads questions, needs the frequency scale re-explained, discloses out of order. Tests whether the agent can actively guide rather than merely transcribe.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What is your full legal name as it appears on your legal documents?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Um—my name? I mean, I’m Douglas, that’s what I usually go by. If you mean the paperwork kind of name, I’m not sure if you want the whole thing all at once… could you say it another way?

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: How would you like your gender recorded?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Male.

conversation.speaker: PATIENT

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Please repeat your 10-digit phone number.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Do you currently have a family doctor?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Hmm, family doctor… I think so, yes, but I’m not sure if you mean the regular doctor I see or something else? I’ve got one I go to, but if you want the exact wording I might need you to ask it another way.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Please answer yes or no.

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Yes.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What is your family doctor's full first and last name?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Oh—his name… I’m blanking on the full thing just now. It’s Dr. S… something. Siddiqui, I think? Or Siddiqi? I’d want to check before I give the exact first and last name.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Do you currently have a psychiatrist?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: No.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What main problems or difficulties have you been experiencing lately?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Mostly it’s the sleep, really. I’ve been having trouble getting off to sleep for about seven months now, ever since my shift pattern changed, and then I’m tired through the day because of it. My mood’s been okay otherwise, more or less stable.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What do you hope to get out of your appointment?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: I just want to sleep properly again, without having to rely on anything… that’s really the main thing.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Have you ever been assessed by a mental health professional?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Yes, back in 2009 I was seen by a hospital psychiatry team after an overdose during my divorce. It was a rough time, but that was a long time ago.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: When were you assessed, and by whom?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: In 2009, by a hospital psychiatry team… at the hospital, after the overdose. I’m not sure how else to put it.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Have you ever received a psychiatric diagnosis, such as depression, anxiety, OCD, or bipolar disorder? If yes, please list the diagnoses.

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Yes — major depressive disorder, single episode, in full remission.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Have you ever been admitted to a hospital for mental health reasons?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Yes, I was admitted in 2009 after the overdose. It was at Scarborough General Hospital, and I stayed there for four days.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What year was it, where were you admitted, and how long was the stay?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: 2009, Scarborough General Hospital, four days.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Have you ever thought about or tried to intentionally hurt yourself?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Yes, there was an intentional overdose in 2009 during my divorce. Since then, nothing—no self-harm thoughts or suicidal thoughts at all for fifteen years.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Have you previously received CBT, DBT, interpersonal therapy, mindfulness-based therapy, psychodynamic therapy, or another therapy?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Yes — CBT, cognitive behavioural therapy. I had it around 2010, about 12 sessions, at a community clinic.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: When did you receive that therapy?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Around 2010.

conversation.speaker: CIRA

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: About 12 sessions.

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: I don’t know of any, no — nothing like that comes to mind.

conversation.speaker: CIRA

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: No, not currently.

conversation.speaker: CIRA

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Yes — citalopram.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What was the name of the past psychiatric medication?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Citalopram.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What dose did you take?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: 20 mg daily.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: When did you start and stop it, or approximately how long did you take it?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: About 18 months from 2009, and then I stopped after I’d recovered well enough.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Why was it discontinued?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: It was stopped after sustained recovery.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Were there any other past psychiatric medications? If yes, please give the medication name.

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: No, those are all.

conversation.message: Have you ever been diagnosed with any medical conditions?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Yes — type 2 diabetes. It was diagnosed in 2018.

conversation.speaker: CIRA

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Type 2 diabetes.

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
